test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Foundational Full Test - 01
subject: general
question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 80 km/h and 120 km/h. The length of one train time is 300 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 12 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed of trains = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h = 200 × (5/18) = 500/9 m/s.

Total distance covered in 12 seconds = Speed × Time = (500/9) × 12 = 2000/3 m = 666.67 m.

Length of the other train = Total Distance − Length of first train.

Length of the other train = 666.67 − 300 = 366.67 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 366.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 120 km/h

Length of first train (L₁) = 300 m

Time taken to cross each other (T) = 12 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

 
• 
 
 L1 = 300 m
 80 km/h →
 
 L2 = x m
 ← 120 km/h
 Opposite Direction ⇒ Relative Speed = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h
 Time to Cross = 12 s

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 200 × (5/18) = 1000/18 = 500/9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ 300 + L₂ = (500/9) × 12

⇒ 300 + L₂ = 500 × (4/3) = 2000/3

⇒ L₂ = (2000/3) − 300

⇒ L₂ = (2000 − 900) ÷ 3

⇒ L₂ = 1100 ÷ 3 ≈ 366.67 m

**∴ The correct answer is 366.67 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction with speeds u and v (where u > v), their relative speed is (u − v).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train of length L crosses a stationary point object like a pole or a standing man, the distance covered is exactly equal to the length of the train L. Time taken = L ÷ Speed of the train.
